playerToWatchData.name: Patrik Schick
playerToWatchData.bio: Schick’s goalscoring gift was obvious from a very young age. Playing for Vestec, a village near Prague, he didn’t celebrate his goals, said coaches, but would instead just pick the ball up, take it to the centre circle and ask for the game to be resumed. When he missed a big chance, he would cry and had to be substituted. Aged eight he was inspired by watching Wayne Rooney play for Manchester United at Sparta Prague. He recalled: “I thought that I want to do this – never get a normal job, and earn a living like him.” It worked out well. He played a grand total of 36 league minutes in Sparta Prague’s first team before Sampdoria decided they had seen enough, paying €4m for the gangly 20-year-old. He signed for Roma a year later in a move that could have been worth up to a club record €42m, but it didn’t really work out there: he ended up on the wing, was loaned to Leipzig, then was sold to Leverkusen in 2020 for €26.5m - which is where everything clicked. In April this year, he scored his 100th goal for them in all competitions. He helped Czechia qualify for the first time in 20 years via the playoffs. He was 10 when they last played at a World Cup. “I vividly remember the games. The Czech fans have waited a long time for this.”

Czechia.strengths: The spine of the side has plenty of experience, led by Soucek in midfield, while Schick scored 16 Bundesliga goals this season.
Czechia.weaknesses: A serious lack of technical players, with the team relying too heavily on physicality, work rate, aggression and set pieces.
Czechia.bio: Having squeezed in via the playoffs, Koubek’s well-drilled side have hopes of advancing from a middling group. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/czechia-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Raúl Jiménez
playerToWatchData.bio: After the skull fracture in 2020 that threatened his career and forced him out of the game for eight months, Raúl Jiménez re-emerged with a protective headband and a completely different outlook. “I almost lost everything, even my life. So I’m trying to enjoy football as much as I can,” he explained. “Everything, not just football. Everything I try to enjoy more.” In England he’s admired for his composure and link-up play, but his story carries more weight than goals alone. But there has been some criticism of late, amid poor results for the national team and a personal goal drought (penalties excepted) – he has criticised fans for booing, while José Ramón Fernández, the doyen of Mexican football journalism, recently named him the most overrated player in the setup.

Mexico.strengths: Flexible tactics, a tight defensive unit and an approach based on intensity, aggressive pressing and quick transitions.
Mexico.weaknesses: Pressure as co-hosts could affect even an experienced squad, while Aguirre’s pragmatic approach has drawn criticism.
Mexico.bio: Playing in a third World Cup on home soil, El Tri are competitive and flexible but may struggle to meet fans’ high expectations. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/mexico-world-cup-2026-team-guide-soccer).

playerToWatchData.name: Teboho Mokoena
playerToWatchData.bio: One of South Africa’s most essential players since Hugo Broos was appointed manager in May 2021. “Tebza” is as solid as they come in midfield, with pinpoint passing, long-range shots and relentless work rate. He is also a free-kick specialist. Like captain Ronwen Williams, he came up through the ranks at SuperSport United, before joining Sundowns. During qualification for the 2026 World Cup he was at the centre of a scandal which almost cost South Africa a place in the finals when he unwittingly played in a 2-0 win over Lesotho despite being suspended. Fifa handed Lesotho a 3-0 walkover, fined South Africa’s FA £9,300 and issued Mokoena with a warning. He spoke about it last year, telling Radio 2000 about the abuse he and his family had received: “I knew [it would happen] on social media, but when it happened twice at the mall, that’s when it hit me hard. When it happened face-to-face I knew I was going to regret it for the rest of my life … I didn’t even know that I had those yellow cards, so it was very difficult, and I was relieved when we qualified for the World Cup. I was not happy but relieved. It was a tough few months for me, and I was not myself at home … The coach said I shouldn’t blame myself and that we’re all involved and we should have all known.”

South-Africa.strengths: International setup revitalised under Broos, knitted together by Mokoena in midfield, and built on well-drilled teamwork.
South-Africa.weaknesses: A squad mainly made up of domestic players lacks wider experience and will rely heavily on counterattacks to create chances.
South-Africa.bio: Bafana Bafana have emerged from a stagnant period after hosting in 2010 and held off Nigeria in qualifying. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/27/south-africa-world-cup-2026-team-guide-soccer).

playerToWatchData.name: Son Heung-min
playerToWatchData.bio: 2025 was a big year for Son. As the captain who finally broke Tottenham’s trophy curse, he ended a decade in North London with a £20m move to Los Angeles – an MLS record – amid a blizzard of “east versus west” marketing pitting Lionel Messi in the Eastern Conference versus Son in the Western. He remains a superb talent, though there was some criticism in the build-up to the World Cup that he has started losing his edge. Son hit back, saying: “I don't think I've suffered any dip in my performance. It's disappointing that people talk about decline whenever I hit a dry spell. I know there are high expectations on me because I've scored so many goals over the years. I am always doing the best I can, and I am feeling good physically." In 2022 he launched his own fashion brand, NOS7, standing for “Nothing, Ordinary Sunday”, with the brand ethos focused on reflection and calm at the weekend: “Weekend after a busy week, we share that precious moment.”

South-Korea.strengths: With a robust core, the team has a great spirit and a proper talisman in former Premier League golden boot winner Son.
South-Korea.weaknesses: Uncertainty over ideal formation, with a late switch to 3-4-3 during qualifying, plus fears about form and fitness of key players.
South-Korea.bio: The Taegeuk Warriors went unbeaten to qualify for their 11th straight finals, but ambitions do not extend far beyond escaping their group. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/28/south-korea-world-cup-2026-team-guide-soccer).

playerToWatchData.name: Edin Dzeko
playerToWatchData.bio: Long before he became the defining figure in Bosnia and Herzegovina’s football history, Dzeko was sold by Zeljeznicar to Czech side Teplice for a relatively small fee because few people inside Bosnian football truly believed a tall, physically underdeveloped striker from Sarajevo could possibly become one of Europe’s elite forwards. He had grown up playing football between buildings and shelters in Sarajevo during the war, later describing football from that period as “an escape from reality”. What followed became the greatest career Bosnian football has produced. Bundesliga titles with Wolfsburg, Premier League triumphs with Manchester City, captaincy at Roma, Champions League finals with Inter; Dzeko eventually became Bosnia's all-time leading appearance-maker and record goalscorer, and remains one of their key players at the age of 40. Inside Bosnia, though, his importance long ago moved beyond football itself. Younger players in Sergej Barbarez’s squad often speak about him less as a teammate and more as the reference point of an entire generation.

Bosnia-and-Herzegovina.strengths: Aggressive defending, direct, passionate football and quick transitions, plus a huge young talent in Alajbegovic.
Bosnia-and-Herzegovina.weaknesses: Intensity can go too far, with a loss of shape and discipline; unlikely to be able to dominate games in their group.
Bosnia-and-Herzegovina.bio: Surprise qualifiers who stunned Italy in the playoffs, Barbarez’s intense and unpredictable side could win over neutrals. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/28/bosnia-and-herzegovina-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Alphonso Davies
playerToWatchData.bio: When Davies moves his feet, he flies – and it certainly felt like he had wings when he leapt to head home Canada’s first-ever World Cup goal in 2022. “When I ran to the corner flag, I looked to my left and I just saw all my teammates running towards me. When they all came around me, a lot of players were grabbing my jersey, pushing me, shoving me. I had Liam Millar headbutt me at one point, he was so excited. We both looked at each other and started laughing." It made a big impact in the stands, too: his parents, who had fled the civil war in Liberia to Ghana, where Davies was born in a refugee camp, before finding safe haven in Canada, were in the stadium watching. “They told me how proud they are of me and when I scored the goal, my mother teared up a bit. My parents are people of few words, they don't really say too much. But it really showed on their faces.” Back in 2018, aged 17, he gave a speech about his background to Fifa delegates in Moscow as part of the Canadian bid to host this World Cup. Davies then joined Bayern Munich from Vancouver Whitecaps, blossoming into one of the world’s best left-backs, and winning everything available to him along the way.

Canada.strengths: Consistent 4-4-2 approach built on pressing from the front and pace out wide, all backed by a resilient defensive unit.
Canada.weaknesses: Fitness fears over star man Davies, a competitive group and the burden of never having won a World Cup match.
Canada.bio: Marsch has turned the co-hosts into a solid and settled team, and worked to develop the mentality to handle pressure. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/28/canada-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Akram Afif
playerToWatchData.bio: The country’s big star, big hope and the magician on the wing, and not just because he has been known to pull playing cards out of his socks upon scoring. If the two-time Asian Player of the Year plays well, then Qatar have a chance. Did not have the best World Cup in 2022, when hopes were high, and it was also disappointing that he never made it in Europe so this is his big chance to show that he is capable of mixing it with the big boys. Can dribble past defenders and create – there were 10 assists as Qatar won the 2019 Asian Cup – and score: he hit eight goals as Qatar won the 2023 Asian Cup, including a hat-trick in the final. Qatar need Afif to shine.

Qatar.strengths: Hugely experienced coach Lopetegui will put hard focus on soaking up pressure and looking to hit opponents on the break.
Qatar.weaknesses: Defence was a mess in qualifying, conceding 24 times in 10 games in the main section, while regional conflict badly disrupted preparation.
Qatar.bio: The 2022 hosts stumbled through qualifying but could benefit from a much lower profile in these finals. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/29/qatar-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Granit Xhaka
playerToWatchData.bio: Captain, record-breaker and the manager’s right-hand man: Granit Xhaka is the undisputed leader of the national team at his seventh major tournament – both on and off the pitch. In the March friendlies against Germany and Norway, the captain was rested for three quarters of the two matches. “We have to be prepared to play without him at times, or when he is marked man-to-man, as he was against Germany,” said Murat Yakin. After a difficult start to their relationship, the pair are now very close. The midfielder has been around for some time now. In 2011, Ottmar Hitzfeld threw the then 18-year-old Xhaka in at the deep end at Wembley during a Euro qualifier against England and the Under-17 World Cup winner is now the record holder for international caps in his country with more than 140 appearances. Many felt that his career was on the way down when he joined Bayer Leverkusen in 2023 after seven years at Arsenal but it was the opposite - and as Xabi Alonso’s leader on the pitch he took the club to a first ever Bundesliga title, won the Cup and reached the Europa League final. Now back in England, he says: “It’s important for me to experience moments of suffering and solidarity too.” His parents are from Kosovo; his father, Ragip, was arrested in 1986 at the age of 22 during a demonstration against the communist central government

Switzerland.strengths: Comfortable in qualifying, topped their group with a mix of experience and fresh talent knitted together by Xhaka.
Switzerland.weaknesses: Some tactical uncertainty over formation, and big expectations from fans despite their side lacking depth beyond the starting XI.
Switzerland.bio: Yakin is aiming for the 'best World Cup from a Swiss team' as he seeks to turn reliable regulars into contenders this summer. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/29/switzerland-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Vinícius Júnior
playerToWatchData.bio: Almost everyone in Brazil knew what was coming from Viní Jr, right from the start. The hype began when he was a pre-teen at Flamengo, and he delivered. In 2017, at 17, he agreed a £39m move to Real Madrid, where he grew into the symbol of the team’s success post-Cristiano Ronaldo. Form hasn’t always been consistent, including with the Seleção, but if there is one man who knows how to get the best out of him it is Carlo Ancelotti. In 2024, Vinícius said of his then club manager: “He's done everything for me. He's always given me confidence, told me off when I needed it. He cares about me as much as I care about him. He's changed me as a player, not on the pitch, but in the way I think.” He has repeatedly been the victim of racist abuse in La Liga, and has repeatedly spoken out against it. He said in 2024: “I just want to play football but it’s hard to move forward … I feel less and less like playing. But it never crossed my mind [to leave Spain] because if I leave Spain I give the racists exactly what they want.”

Brazil.strengths: Built around Vinícius, the team has a solid spine which allows room for attacking flair in an aggressive 4-2-4 formation.
Brazil.weaknesses: The full-backs do not match up to former greats, while 34-year-old Neymar may struggle to contribute fully due to injuries.
Brazil.bio: Five-time champions have turned to Ancelotti, who has built an attacking side eager to end years of underachievement. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/29/brazil-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Wilson Isidor
playerToWatchData.bio: Isidor was the boy in Rennes who chased football like it owed him something, darting between cars on makeshift alleyway pitches, celebrating imaginary goals. Tall and quick with a predator’s instinct, he is equally dangerous in the air and on the turn, blending force with surprising grace. His journey took him from Monaco’s youth ranks to trophies in Russia with Zenit St Petersburg, where he lifted league and cup silverware before sprinting into Sunderland’s attack. He had represented France through the age levels but in March, Haiti finally got its man, Isidor confirming his long-awaited decision on social media: “I’ve seen all your messages … you asked for me, you waited for me, and here I am.” He made his full debut against Iceland, and scored his first goal in the same game. He brings real pedigree to Haiti’s forward line, the promise not just of goals but the ignition of a nation’s World Cup dream.

Haiti.strengths: Migné has built a disciplined side with the pace and skill to counter effectively, with Bellegarde and Isidor bringing proven quality.
Haiti.weaknesses: Instability has affected the team’s buildup, with key striker Nazon held up in Iran and Migné unable to visit the country he coaches.
Haiti.bio: Grenadiers will be group outsiders after reaching their first World Cup since 1974 despite turmoil at home. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/30/haiti-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Achraf Hakimi
playerToWatchData.bio: Last year’s African footballer of the year, Hakimi is considered the best right-back in the game and perhaps the first Moroccan superstar. But off the pitch the 27-year-old confirmed in February that he would face trial after being accused of rape in 2023 He denies the allegations. "Today, a rape accusation is enough to justify a trial," Hakimi said on social media. "This is as unjust to the innocent as it is to the genuine victims. I calmly await this trial, which will allow the truth to come out publicly." One of the key players of PSG’s first Champions League title in 2025, Hakimi still has a close friendship with Kylian Mbappé, his former teammate now at Real Madrid. “He was the one who helped me with my French when I first got to Paris,” he said.

Morocco.strengths: Ouahbi’s setup will create space for star player Hakimi, while reaching the last four in 2022 has boosted collective belief.
Morocco.weaknesses: The Afcon hosts struggled to cope under pressure, culminating in a farcical final, and will be under close scrutiny again this summer.
Morocco.bio: Atlas Lions made history as Africa’s first semi-finalists in Qatar and expect to make a similar impact after a recent coaching change. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/30/morocco-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Scott McTominay
playerToWatchData.bio: Did he launch himself 8ft, 18ft or 88ft into the air before planting an outrageous overhead kick beyond the reach of Kasper Schmeichel? Who cares? McTominay’s opening goal against Denmark set the tone for a remarkable night as Scotland ended almost three decades of World Cup hurt. Alex McLeish’s greatest gift to his nation during a second spell as the Scotland manager was convincing McTominay to don navy blue. Without McLeish’s refusal to take no for an answer, the Lancaster-born McTominay could be an England player by now. Instead, he is idolised by the Tartan Army. There is lauding, too, in Naples, after he was part of the 2024-25 Scudetto winning squad. “If Diego was God, then Scott is Jesus,” insisted Diego Maradona Jnr, in reference to the status both his father and McTominay have secured in the eyes of Napoli fans. McTominay will arrive at the World Cup with a point to prove, having disappointed in Euro 2024.

Scotland.strengths: Built around key lieutenants like McTominay and Robertson, Scotland’s first-choice XI is organised and hugely experienced.
Scotland.weaknesses: The team lacks a reliable scorer, with Clarke often criticised for his caution, while Billy Gilmour’s injury will hurt a squad lacking depth.
Scotland.bio: Clarke’s side ended 28-year wait to qualify in cathartic style and will seek to reward travelling fans with a first trip to the knockouts. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/30/scotland-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Jackson Irvine
playerToWatchData.bio: The Australia midfield leader plays with the calm authority and tactical nous of someone who has seen the grind of the lower leagues and now relishes playing on the grandest stages for club and country. Born and raised in Melbourne, battle-hardened in Scotland and England, Irvine is thriving in Germany. Since arriving at St Pauli in 2021, he has become the heartbeat of their midfield, the club captain, and a key player in their return to the German top tier. The promotion celebrations were so wild that Irvine forgot to take his passport to his own wedding two days later. The otherwise thoughtful and articulate Socceroo is not afraid to express his political and social views and, in April, hit out at Fifa for awarding a peace prize to Donald Trump. “As an organisation, you would have to say decisions like the one that we saw awarding this peace prize makes a mockery of what they’re trying to do with the human rights charter,” he said. Yet a lighter side hides in plain sight, with Irvine’s many tattoos including one on his right leg of Simpsons character Moe Szyslak.

Australia.strengths: Popovic improved the team in qualifying and has made them tougher to beat, while Irankunda leads a dangerous counterattacking unit.
Australia.weaknesses: The new coach is eager to shake off the ‘underdogs’ tag, but it may prove tough with a lack of high-profile names in a transitional squad.
Australia.bio: At their sixth successive finals, the Socceroos arrive with an experienced core, young attacking talent and designs on a first knockout win. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/01/australia-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Julio Enciso
playerToWatchData.bio: “Dear grandpa, I dedicate this to you in heaven with all my heart. I always remember when you pointed at me and told me that one day I would be there,” Enciso wrote emotionally, as Paraguay sealed their return to the World Cup. Enciso made the promise to become a professional player to save his family from poverty. He pledged to play for his country – he was only 17 when that was ticked off – and promised that his grandfather would see him playing in a World Cup. That second promise was not to be, as his grandfather passed away before Julio had played for his country. He made his debut at Libertad in the Paraguayan first division aged only 15 and moved to Europe at 18, signing for Brighton. He joined Strasbourg last summer, and is now established as Paraguay’s top attacker, offering flair, dribbling, assists and goals.

Paraguay.strengths: La Albirroja will rely on the assets that saw them through qualifying: playing a physical style with the tenacity to dig out unlikely results.
Paraguay.weaknesses: Only two teams scored fewer goals in Conmebol qualifying and there may be an over-reliance on Enciso to create and take chances.
Paraguay.bio: Alfaro has rebuilt the team around 'Paraguayan DNA – intensity and clean sheets' and hopes of progress are high after 12 years away. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/31/paraguay-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Arda Guler
playerToWatchData.bio: “The last time we were able to go to the World Cup, I didn’t even exist,” Guler said after Turkey had qualified for the tournament for the first time since 2002 – and the Real Madrid man is the undisputed face of this side. After proving himself at one of the biggest clubs in the world and shining for the national team he is now preparing to take centre stage in his biggest test yet. “We are talking about an undisputed, elite world-class talent,” is how Thierry Henry recently described the Turkish attacking midfielder. The 21-year-old may have a babyface but he is no pushover and not a luxury player. The midfielder was involved in a staggering 44 percent of the Red-Whites goals in games he played in for the 2025-26 qualifying campaign and he showed his passion and precociousness in the Champions League quarter-final away leg against Bayern. First he scored an outrageous long-range goal in the first minute, then a second within half an hour before getting sent off in added-on time for dissent.

Turkey.strengths: Montella has built a harmonious squad with in-form players and two of Europe’s brightest attacking talents in the shape of Guler and Yildiz.
Turkey.weaknesses: Lack of a proven striker and big-game experience in some areas increases the risk of the wheels coming off as they did at Euro 2020.
Turkey.bio: After a remarkable 22-year absence following their third-place finish in 2002, Montella's talented squad are primed to make an impact on their return to the world stage. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/31/turkey-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Christian Pulisic
playerToWatchData.bio: This generation of USA players has more than ever playing at elite clubs in Europe, but none of them are as important to the team’s success as Pulisic. When he is on form, “the kid from Hershey, Pennsylvania” is more capable than anyone in the team of finding a way through defences, and finding small windows in which to take shots and, ideally, score goals. In 2025, he said “his body had started talking to him” and he opted out of the Gold Cup squad, a decision he was criticised for by certain former players, such as Landon Donovan and Tim Howard. “When it comes to [Donovan, Howard, and other ex-national team critics], it is tough because I looked up to those guys growing up,” he told CBS. “Some of these guys were my idols, and I respect them so much as players. Privately, the way they talk to me and clearly want to show support and be your friend and everything, and then they say something slightly different publicly. Does it hurt me? Am I surprised by it? I don’t know. Not really.” Though he’s surrounded by a more than capable USA roster, the pressure on Pulisic to perform at this World Cup is immense. He is the face of the program, even if he himself is more of an introvert.

USA.strengths: The core of the squad are ‘glue guys’ with prior World Cup experience, while their head coach knows how to win knockout matches.
USA.weaknesses: Pochettino still seems unclear on his best team and tactical setup, leaving many home fans frustrated before a ball has been kicked.
USA.bio: Expectations are low for the co-hosts after a turbulent buildup, but there is a path to the latter stages if Pochettino can harness his team’s abilities. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/31/usa-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Nicolas Pépé
playerToWatchData.bio: “The World Cup is a childhood dream,” Pépé said recently. “It’s the biggest competition in world football. I’m 30 now and I think this will be my only chance to play in one because there’s no guarantee I’ll be in the national team by the time I’m 34.” After playing at four Afcons and failing to qualify for two World Cups, the winger faces the challenge of his life. The skilled dribbler remains one of the key players of this Côte d’Ivoire side – and one of the loudest voices. A big presence in the dressing room, Pépé often shares videos of his teammates on social media. The former Arsenal winger is serious about playing for the national team too: “I have given my head for this team by shaving my Mohican since Under-17 level,” he said, a way of showing his respect for the badge.

Cote-dIvoire.strengths: Faé’s defence is settled but still flexible and did not concede in qualifying, and the coach has a wealth of attacking talent at his disposal.
Cote-dIvoire.weaknesses: There are questions over midfield selection and their underwhelming Afcon defence has lowered previously high expectations this summer.
Cote-dIvoire.bio: The Elephants believe they can do what their golden generation failed to: reach the knockout stages, or as Faé has said: ‘Why not win it?’ [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/01/cote-divoire-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Leandro Bacuna
playerToWatchData.bio: One of the squad’s most capped - and experienced - players as he chose to represent Curaçao back in 2016, while he was still playing in the Premier League with Aston Villa. Patrick Kluivert was the head coach then and Bacuna followed in the footsteps of the goalkeeper Eloy Room, who had opted to play for Curaçao the year before. The team became incredibly close-knit, something reflected in how they honour Jairzinho Pieter, a former national team goalkeeper who died while travelling with the squad. Pieter was known for leading the team’s daily prayers – a ritual still observed today, with Bacuna placing a necklace belonging to him at the centre of the team huddle. “His passing was very difficult at the time and it is still very difficult,” Room said. “That made the dream of reaching the World Cup come even more to life, because it was also truly his dream. It gave us even more motivation.”

Curacao.strengths: Advocaat’s return is a huge bonus; the vastly experienced head coach has led the team’s improvement and brought in players from the island’s diaspora.
Curacao.weaknesses: The team’s possession-based style may need to be overhauled in a tough group, and kicking off against Germany is a particularly daunting test.
Curacao.bio: The smallest nation by population and area to reach a World Cup, Advocaat’s side will seek to make a splash beyond their surprise qualification. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/01/curacao-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Moisés Caicedo
playerToWatchData.bio: From Santo Domingo's dusty pitches to breaking the British transfer record, Caicedo is on quite a journey. When Chelsea paid Brighton £115m in 2023 they gave him an eight-year contract, a huge financial show of confidence in his ability. And, after what he called “a difficult start, I felt the pressure”, he has lived up to that billing at Stamford Bridge. A calm, sensitive character, his childhood nickname “Niño Moi” – “The Boy Moi” – has stuck, and he launched his Niño Moi 23 Academy in Guayas last year, saying he hoped it would “shape both sporting talents and exemplary citizens, grounded in good values”. Faith drives him: “I pray at every match, win or lose … I ask God to see us through each match without injuries.” He arrived at the World Cup carrying over a suspension following his red card in last year’s qualifier against Argentina, a match which began with his mum, Carmen, walking out to deliver the matchball to the referee.

Ecuador.strengths: A defence marshalled by Pacho and Hincapié conceded just five goals in 18 qualifiers and Beccacece has introduced a Bielsa-esque pressing mentality.
Ecuador.weaknesses: Scoring remains a problem and beyond veteran striker Enner Valencia, attacking options are talented but raw and unproven at the highest level.
Ecuador.bio: At their fifth World Cup, this may be El Tri’s strongest squad, seeking to win their first knockout game after qualifying in impressive fashion. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/02/ecuador-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Florian Wirtz
playerToWatchData.bio: In Germany, Wirtz is known as the player who made Bayer Leverkusen’s miraculous league and cup double in 2024 possible, ending Bayern Munich’s long-standing dominance. He has also shone for Germany, including a sensational performance in the 4-3 victory against Switzerland in March, but his major breakthrough is yet to come. Has had an up-and-down first season at Anfield after his £100m transfer last summer with his manager Arne Slot saying things will only get better. “Full credit to Wirtz on the pitch and the gym, putting in the work,” the Dutchman says. “If someone is struggling physically at the start, you have to keep them in to improve and he was an example of that.” When his pre‑Euro 2024 ranking of potato dishes on the German football federation’s TikTok account went viral (he put a “normal” potato at No 1 to much public amusement), he responded: “I don’t find it entertaining at all.” At the World Cup it still remains to be seen whether he will be given the central role his talent warrants.

Germany.strengths: A blend of rising stars and reliable stalwarts, this squad has more than enough creative talent to take advantage of a decent group-stage draw.
Germany.weaknesses: This is not yet a vintage Germany side and results have been inconsistent, while Neuer is back in goal after a reliable successor could not be found.
Germany.bio: Winners in 2014, Die Mannschaft crashed out at the group stage in the last two finals but have rebuilt well under tactical obsessive Nagelsmann. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/02/germany-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Takefusa Kubo
playerToWatchData.bio: A huge talent, often dubbed “the Japanese Messi”. Kubo was talent spotted by Barcelona at the age of eight, and joined their La Masia academy at 10. In 2023 he revealed how hard the experience had been, saying: “There were a lot of kids with strong personalities at school and in the dorms, so I tried not to get lost in the crowd, or rather, I thought that if I was looked down upon even a little, it would be the end, so even though I was small I tried my best not to lose, but I still got punched by bigger kids. I can't really say much, but it was a really tough environment.” His progress there was halted, anyway, when the club was found to have violated Fifa international transfer policy for Under-18s. Instead he developed at FC Tokyo before returning to Spain with Real Madrid in 2019. His ability to draw in defenders with sharp, explosive dribbling makes him a huge threat, and he is equally potent as a playmaker, delivering decisive final passes. He has plenty of self-confidence too, saying recently: “I’m not just good with the ball at my feet – I think I’m good at football as a whole.” This summer is a chance to showcase his talents on a global stage, with clubs in England tracking his progress.

Japan.strengths: Samurai Blue play as a cohesive unit, pressing from the front in Moriyasu’s settled system, and now have the squad depth to make a deeper run.
Japan.weaknesses: Injury to Kaoru Mitoma is a blow and they have landed in a tough group with three experienced and physical opponents.
Japan.bio:
Perennial dark horses capable of causing shocks, impressive warm-up results have fuelled belief they can break new ground by reaching the quarter-finals.
 [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/02/japan-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Virgil van Dijk
playerToWatchData.bio: Uefa has handed out the European Footballer of the Year award since 2011. Only once has the prestigious prize gone to a defender – in 2019, when Virgil van Dijk beat Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. “I had to work hard for every step of the way – that's part of me and I'm very happy about that,” he said as he accepted the award. “I'm very proud, it's all credit to everyone that's helped me along the way.” The son of a Surinamese mother and Dutch father, he was initially criticised in the youth ranks at Willem II after being deemed too “laid-back”. Via FC Groningen, Celtic and Southampton, he arrived at Liverpool in 2018. A proper leader for club and country, even though in the Netherlands he still rarely gets the credit he deserves, being held in higher esteem in England. That’s not true back at Willem II, though, where they named a stand after him at their Sportpark Prinsenhoeve youth facility in Tilburg last year. The club said: “With this, his name is not only immortalised in the rich history of Willem II, but also emphatically linked to the development of youth football in the city.”

Netherlands.strengths: The Oranje smashed in 27 goals to qualify unbeaten, but it is their back four which looks most impressive on paper, marshalled by captain Van Dijk.
Netherlands.weaknesses: Several key players have suffered from injury layoffs or lack of game time this season, and facing Japan first will test this team’s cohesion.
Netherlands.bio:
Koeman has been set a target of reaching the semi-finals, but has been forced to prioritise strength and fitness over skill with a raft of injury issues.
 [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/03/netherlands-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Alexander Isak
playerToWatchData.bio: “It was magical, they sang for me.” On 21 September 2016, Alexander Isak turned 17 and became a derby hero. He scored two goals against fierce rivals Djurgården (in a 3-0 win) and was serenaded with a birthday song by the supporters. A super talent who  has gone from strength to strength and last year became the most expensive player in Premier League history. Despite being at the top, is described as a calm and humble person who hasn’t forgotten his roots. Thania Guanoluisa, his Spanish teacher in school, received a call from him when he was playing for Real Sociedad: “Alexander said: ‘Thania, it was you who gave me the foundations in Spanish.’ I was so happy that he remembered and appreciated it.” Enraged Newcastle fans after going on strike to force a move to Liverpool and his first campaign at Anfield has been one to forget because of injuries. Remains a key player for Sweden regardless.

Sweden.strengths: Potter has two elite finishers at his disposal up front but will set up with a hard-working back five to complement the firepower in his squad.
Sweden.weaknesses: Isak endured a grim first season at Liverpool, and Potter has had limited time to apply his methods after taking over last October.
Sweden.bio: Took two points from 18 in a disastrous qualifying campaign, but grasped their playoff chance under Potter and have the attacking talent to go further. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/03/sweden-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Hannibal Mejbri
playerToWatchData.bio: Without a doubt, the biggest star of the Tunisian national team. In 2021, the national FA organised a special press conference to officially present Mejbri, in a first for a dual-nationality player choosing Tunisia. The young midfielder was emerging at Manchester United and had been capped by France at youth level, but said: “My heart chose Tunisia. You do not choose a national team by default or keep a country waiting.” Not only is Mejbri a star on the pitch, but he also speaks with remarkable maturity, something that greatly appeals to Tunisian fans. Following Tunisia’s surprise elimination against Mali at Afcon 2025, he criticised the state of football development in Tunisia. “We dream a lot, but we do not work enough. We do not educate ourselves. We must ask ourselves serious questions because we have fallen far behind.” Now at Burnley, the playmaker who earned comparisons with David Beckham while at United’s academy, always stood out, as one of them said: “He had a unique style, with big blond hair. Where you could find a pitch and a ball, you would find Hannibal.”

Tunisia.strengths: Did not concede a goal in qualifying and have been tactically flexible under Lamouchi, who has pleased supporters with his desire to bring young talent through.
Tunisia.weaknesses: Burnley’s Mejbri is the creative star of a low-key team lacking elite experience, who may find it difficult to play with freedom in a challenging group.
Tunisia.bio: After six World Cups and six group-stage exits, the Eagles of Carthage seek to break new ground with an imposing team drawn from the country’s diaspora. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/03/tunisia-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Kevin De Bruyne
playerToWatchData.bio: What do Jamal Musiala, Gavi and Anthony Gordon have in common? They all played in the KDB Cup, the now 10-year-old prestigious youth tournament named after (and supported by) Kevin De Bruyne. His own younger years – back when he frequently ran away from training because of arguments with coaches, was supporting Liverpool and went on a trial at Arsenal – seem a long time ago now. He arrives at the World Cup as an elder statesman, a Manchester City legend, with 422 games, 108 goals and 19 trophies, and one of Belgium’s last “golden generation” members. He certainly hopes to perform better than at the previous World Cup. If not, he’ll be flying home on his 35th birthday, since it falls right after the New Zealand game. But whatever happens, the family’s future looks bright after footage emerged of his seven-year-old son Rome scoring some of his dad’s trademark goals at Real Casarea, a club in the Napoli area.

Belgium.strengths: De Bruyne, Doku and Lukaku offer a serious attacking edge, though the latter played only 64 minutes for Napoli this season.
Belgium.weaknesses: The defence is, except for Courtois, the weak point with the golden generation of Alderweireld, Kompany, Vermaelen and Vertonghen long gone.
Belgium.bio: A time of transition for the Red Devils. Qualifying went smoothly but was never particularly eye-catching.  [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/04/belgium-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Mohamed Salah
playerToWatchData.bio: The Egyptian King needs little introduction, and his career has become a permanent argument against ceilings. In December, he became the player with the most goal involvements at a single club in Premier League history, with 277, surpassing Wayne Rooney. No one has won more Golden Boot awards in the league’s history than his four (joint-top with Thierry Henry), and he is the highest scoring foreign player in the league. Salah has led Egypt to two Africa Cup of Nations finals in 2017 and 2021, and he was named in the team of the tournament on each run. His defining national team moment, however, remains the stoppage time penalty against Congo in October 2017 that sent Egypt to the 2018 World Cup and ended a 28-year absence from the competition. Since announcing that he will call time on his storied nine-year spell at Liverpool, he has played with a certain freedom, despite not being at his best this season. Salah has scored 65 international goals at the time of writing, second on his country’s all-time list and chasing the record held by Hossam Hassan, Egypt's head coach. As captain and the focal point of the squad, he remains the player around whom successive coaches have built their plans.

Egypt.strengths: Cohesive, often hard to score against and emotionally committed.
Egypt.weaknesses: Can look blunt if opponents double up on Salah and the midfield cannot pass through the press.
Egypt.bio: Salah led the way through qualifying but limitations of the side were exposed at Afcon, where Senegal inflicted a semi-final defeat. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/04/egypt-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Mehdi Taremi
playerToWatchData.bio: For years, it looked like Mehdi Taremi would be better known for off-field shenanigans – a four-month global ban from football related to a contract dispute with Turkish club Rizespor, a relationship with the famous Iranian actress Sahar Ghoreyshi – than for anything he might do on the pitch. But his move to Portuguese club Rio Ave in 2019 changed everything, and he later went to Porto and Inter, where he was able to fully showcase his abilities. He won league and cup titles with Porto and reached the Champions League final with Inter, while his spectacular bicycle kick for Porto against Chelsea was nominated for the Puskás Award and voted Goal of the Season in the Champions League. Taremi is a striker who excels at running behind defensive lines, and even minimal contact is often enough for him to go down and win penalties – a trait that has earned him a controversial reputation in Portugal. He is Iran’s captain and star. With two goals against England in the 2022 World Cup, he is already Iran’s all-time top scorer in the tournament.

Iran.strengths: Capable of mixing things up – in March friendlies they played a 3-6-1 against Nigeria and a 4-4-2 against Costa Rica.
Iran.weaknesses: Ghalenoei and his staff will have to work hard to minimise disruption for the squad, which will be based in Mexico but will play three group games in the US.
Iran.bio: Smooth sailing in qualifying – anything but easy since then. The conflict with the United States threw their involvement into doubt but Ghalenoei's side are all set to compete. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/04/iran-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Chris Wood
playerToWatchData.bio: What Ronaldo is for Portugal, Wood is for the All Whites  - goalscorer and endlessly loyal to his country, so fans have been fretting about his fitness in the World Cup buildup. An inspiration for youngsters, he’s “the poster boy of the All Whites, he's definitely the standout”, RNZ journalist Matthew Nash wrote before the knee injury that derailed his latest Premier League season. Wood had an outstanding campaign in 2024-25, becoming the first Forest player in 30 years to score 20 plus goals in a season and the first Kiwi to be voted Premier League player of the month. The youngest ever All Whites captain says: “Playing for my country makes me extremely proud and honoured.” Returned from knee surgery in April and is hopeful of staying at the top for some time: “I'm not one with blistering pace, so I'm never gonna lose it. So that's good coming into my older years where I can actually still continue to do what I did when I was 22 years old.”

New-Zealand.strengths: There's no shortage of optimism – within the camp there's belief they can to make the knockout rounds for the first time.
New-Zealand.weaknesses: Star striker Wood has had an injury-plagued 2026 and recent friendly results have been mixed at best.
New-Zealand.bio: The All Whites are the lowest-ranked team at the tournament but the squad has evolved from part-timers to professionals. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/05/new-zealand-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Dailon Livramento
playerToWatchData.bio: Some people are destined for greatness and Livramento was one of them. The son of Cape Verdean musical icon Marizia do Rosario, Livramento made his singing debut as a one-year-old when his baby talk was featured in Marizia’s song Daily dedicated to him. The forward himself sings and his brother Jerzy is part of Dutch hip-hop group Broederliefde. Despite only being called up for the first time in 2024 he has already notched seven goals for The Blue Sharks, four of them crucial in qualifying, including both of the goals that sent Cape Verde to the World Cup against Cameroon and Eswatini. “When I scored I pointed to my wrist,” he told the Guardian after the match about his now iconic celebration. “It’s time to go to the World Cup.” In Daily, Marizia describes Livramento as her “everything in the world,” little did she know that he would come to mean just as much to the rest of her tiny island homeland.

Cape-Verde.strengths: A settled squad has been together for the best part of half a decade. Physical and happy to defend but blessed with technical forwards too.
Cape-Verde.weaknesses: Key defender Logan Costa has been out with an anterior cruciate ligament injury all season
Cape-Verde.bio: An eclectic group of players, the Blue Sharks are swimming in completely uncharted waters as they make their World Cup debut. [Read the team guide here](https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/05/cape-verde-world-cup-2026-team-guide).

playerToWatchData.name: Salem Al-Dawsari
playerToWatchData.bio: His winner and somersault against Argentina was one of the moments of the 2022 World Cup and he has continued to be one of the standouts in the star-studded Saudi Pro League thanks to his creativity and vision . There are concerns however, that his national team form is not what it was and a number of missed penalties in qualification almost cost Saudi Arabia a place at the World Cup. When the going gets tough, however, the 2025 Asian Player of the Year is still the one the others look to.

Saudi-Arabia.strengths: Expectations are low, so to some extent the pressure is off. Expect Donis to focus his efforts on defensive solidity.
Saudi-Arabia.weaknesses: The team looks toothless up front: just seven goals were scored in 10 games in the main round of qualification.
Saudi-Arabia.bio: The Green Falcons have had a chaotic buildup to the tournament, with Donis taking charge in April after the bitter exit of Hervé Renard.

playerToWatchData.name: Lamine Yamal
playerToWatchData.bio: Spanish football’s rising star has become one of world football’s superstars. After finishing second in the Ballon d’Or standings to Ousmane Dembélé last year the Barcelona winger was already setting his sights on the top prize. Despite winning his second consecutive league title, it has not been a straightforward season for the 18-year-old, who caused a spat with Real Madrid before and after last October’s clásico and has missed spells – including the final weeks of the campaign – with injury. However, there’s no doubt now that he is Barcelona and Spain’s talisman. If he avoids further fitness issues and leads La Roja to glory in North America, he will be many people’s pick for this year’s Ballon d’Or. The son of a Guinean mother and a Moroccan father, Yamal has broken records throughout his career, including becoming the youngest person to play and to score for Spain at 16 years and 57 days.

Spain.strengths: Lamine Yamal and Williams have injected freshness into a team that still dominates the ball. The frontline will be hard to contain.
Spain.weaknesses: Are there any? The back four can have its moments but this is simply a fiercely competitive and united team.
Spain.bio: Rightly among the favourites. De la Fuente has the perfect blend of youth and experience, prodigious talent and maturity.

playerToWatchData.name: Federico Valverde
playerToWatchData.bio: One of the world’s best had humble beginnings. He doesn’t like admitting it, simply saying his parents “were very hard-working”. He would accompany his mother to her market stall and started playing football so young that he was still wearing nappies. When he arrived at Real Madrid in 2016 feeling like “Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi put together”, he was self-conscious when comparing his clothes with those of his peers. “You’re wearing a €2 T-shirt,” he said to himself. Ironically for a player who used to annoy his youth coaches because he didn’t like running, the midfielder has risen up the ranks at Madrid thanks to his outstanding physical attributes. He scored on debut for Uruguay aged 19 but missed out on the World Cup in 2018, which was a blow. He arrives at this one as his country’s talisman. A hat-trick against Manchester City in the Champions League in March confirmed his elite status. His 2025-26 season ended on a low, however, as he was taken to hospital after an altercation with his Real teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni. In a statement Valverde said: “At no point did my team-mate hit me, and I didn’t hit him either.”

Uruguay.strengths: Brace yourselves for Bielsa-ball: expect La Celeste to press their opponents high up the field and chase the ball at all times.
Uruguay.weaknesses: Uruguay do not have the scoring power of old. Hopes are being pinned on Darwin Núñez, who has struggled for form at Al-Hilal.
Uruguay.bio: The quarter-finals are the aim, but the buildup has been anything but smooth. Bielsa has been under pressure since a 5-1 loss to the USA in November.

playerToWatchData.name: Kylian Mbappé
playerToWatchData.bio: Mbappé is chasing records in North America. Starting the tournament four goals away from Miroslav Klose’s all-time World Cup record of 16, the France forward has an obsession with writing history. However, it is collective titles that drive Mbappé. After winning Ligue 1 in his first full season at Monaco, he piled up the trophies at PSG before joining Real Madrid in 2024. The goals have flowed at Real to the tune of 86 in 103 games, but the major honours have not followed. There was fierce criticism over a trip to Sardinia in May while he recovered from an injury, with some Real fans accusing him of already looking ahead to the World Cup. Club issues aside, Mbappé remains essential for France. The teenager who won the World Cup in 2018 and earned the Golden Boot in the last tournament is now aiming to captain his side to victory this summer.

France.strengths: The front four is a remarkable quartet, and the back four isn't bad either. Their bench might be the strongest at the tournament.
France.weaknesses: A cynic might suggest the head coach's conservatism. More accurately, it's the challenge he faces in putting all the puzzle pieces together.
France.bio: France have attacking talents that are the envy of the world. But will Deschamps take the handbrake off and let them shine?

playerToWatchData.name: Aymen Hussein
playerToWatchData.bio: Hussein is a remarkable footballer with an extraordinary back story. He comes from Hawija, which was one of the most volatile regions in the world after the 2003 US-led invasion of Iraq. His father was killed by Al-Qaeda in 2008, and then in 2014, his brother was abducted by Islamic State; he is presumed dead with his whereabouts still unknown. It was under these dreadful circumstances that the striker began his playing career. Since making his full international debut in 2015, Hussein’s time with Iraq has been a turbulent one. He has faced heavy criticism from fans and the media for his lack of goals. On one occasion, his coach ran on to the pitch to instruct the striker not to take a penalty. However, he is now one of Iraq's five all-time top scorers with 33 goals at the time of writing, the latest being the winner against Bolivia that saw Iraq qualify for their first World Cup in 40 years.

Iraq.strengths: As Arnold says, the pressure is on the other three teams in the group. Iraq have nothing to lose.
Iraq.weaknesses: Not exactly free-scoring. Breaking down three tough defences in the group will be a huge challenge.
Iraq.bio: After a marathon journey to get here (they played 21 qualifiers, more than anyone else) Arnold's side are out to prove they belong on the world stage.

playerToWatchData.name: Erling Haaland
playerToWatchData.bio: It feels almost surreal to think that one of the world’s best footballers grew up in Bryne, a small and unremarkable town in the south-west of Norway. Could it be because people from there work extra hard to get ahead? Is it all the hours spent in the indoor hall that was built because it's difficult to play football outdoors all year round? Maybe it's the fresh milk from the local cows. Perhaps it is because Haaland was so obsessed with football he watched every game he could on TV and even studied Jamie Vardy's ability to stay onside? Or is it because his mother was a prominent heptathlete and his father, Alfie, played in the Premier League? Probably it is a mix of everything. What’s for certain is Haaland’s astonishing goal return – becoming his nation’s all-time top scorer before he turned 25, three Premier League Golden Boots in four seasons at Manchester City, 57 Champions League goals in 58 games – marks him out as a phenomenon and the greatest centre-forward of his era.

Norway.strengths: Haaland will be eager to grab this opportunity on the world stage. The team averaged nearly five goals a game in qualifying.
Norway.weaknesses: Tough group means they have to hit the ground running. First-choice goalkeeper has barely played for his club this season.
Norway.bio: Golden generation vibes for Haaland and friends. But expect Solbakken's side to prioritise effectiveness over aesthetics.

playerToWatchData.name: Sadio Mané
playerToWatchData.bio: Mané is one of the most decorated African players in history. But before winning the Champions League and Premier League with Liverpool, or the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich, he had to batter down some doors. He comes from Bambali, a village from where becoming a pro footballer seemed impossible, and left for an opportunity in Dakar wearing a wrecked pair of football boots – the source of mockery from one coach in his first sessions. Mané’s response became famous: “I am here with the best that I have.” Now a two-time African Player of the Year and the driving force behind Senegal’s first Afcon triumph in 2022, the forward has spent millions building hospitals and schools back home. “I don’t need 10 Ferraris; I want my people to receive a bit of what life has given me,” he has said. A level-headed captain amid the chaos at Afcon earlier this year, the 34-year-old persuaded his teammates to return to the pitch in the final against Morocco.

Senegal.strengths: Thiaw has developed a more flexible tactical approach, while speed in attack will cause teams plenty of problems.
Senegal.weaknesses: Recent tournament record, aside from the most recent Cup of Nations, is unimpressive.
Senegal.bio: The Lions of Teranga arrive in North America in fine shape, thanks to a freshened-up frontline and a defence that is its usual sturdy self. [Read the team guide here](link).

playerToWatchData.name: Riyad Mahrez
playerToWatchData.bio: Very few footballers can match what Mahrez has achieved in the game. Among his accolades, the Algeria captain boasts five Premier League titles, a Champions League winner’s medal, two FA Cups, three League Cups, PFA and CAF player of the year awards, and many other individual and club honours. The only blemish on his career for Algeria fans is that lack of a stellar display at a World Cup. In 2014 his only appearance came in a 2-1 defeat to Belgium where he registered 37 touches, was dispossessed three times and was substituted in the 71st minute. He did not feature again as Algeria surged to the Last 16. Now aged 35 and nearing the twilight of his career, he is determined to lead Algeria into the quarter-finals of the World Cup for the very first time. Such an achievement would elevate his status in African footballing lore. Still, some fans argue that he no longer has the legs to justify a starting place for Algeria, and that it may already be time to hand the mantle to rising talents such as Feyenoord’s Anis Hadj Moussa.

Algeria.strengths: The squad boasts plenty of technical ability and Afcon highlighted just how good they can be at their best.
Algeria.weaknesses: The Afcon quarter-final collapse against Nigeria remains fresh in minds. Was it an aberration or a sign of how this team performs under pressure?
Algeria.bio: One of this World Cup’s great unknowns. Qualifying was a cakewalk – but against generally poor opposition. [Read the team guide here](link).

playerToWatchData.name: Lionel Messi
playerToWatchData.bio: To become the best in the world (and, for many, the greatest in history), Messi had to spend his teenage years away from home. Since Newell's Old Boys couldn’t afford the growth hormone treatment he needed, he moved from Rosario to Barcelona, with his father Jorge, at the age of 13 for a trial. By the time he left to join Paris St-Germain 21 years later, he had won seven Ballons d’Or and the hearts of the world. To his innate talent, he had to add a mental fortitude that proved crucial throughout his career – especially in never giving up after losing finals with the national team, which he endured at the 2014 World Cup and the 2015 and 2016 Copa Américas. This resilience ultimately led him to guide his country to two continental titles and to the pinnacle of success in Qatar. He will turn 39 during the group stage, and is now spending the final years of his professional career at Inter Miami, where he is also part of the club’s ownership group. There, he is surrounded by friends football has given him, such as Luis Suárez, and is enjoying his 'last dance' while helping build a new era for the club, including a stadium that will feature a stand named in his honour.

Argentina.strengths: Almost all of the class of 2022 is still around, including Messi.
Argentina.weaknesses: Several players had injury setbacks at the end of very demanding seasons with their clubs.
Argentina.bio: World Cup and Copa América holders travel with a squad of familiar faces but perhaps not with players in peak physical condition.

playerToWatchData.name: Konrad Laimer
playerToWatchData.bio: Laimer had plenty of doubters when he left RB Leipzig for Bayern Munich on a free transfer in 2023 but, after failing to establish himself as a first-choice midfielder, he has reinvented himself as a right back, occasionally filling in on the left. Laimer is the epitome of a workhorse and, having been educated at Salzburg’s Red Bull academy, the perfect disciple for Ralf Rangnick’s Gegenpressing doctrine. “I want to be as unpleasant as possible on the pitch and I like it when things get physical,” he told Sports Illustrated this year. “One-on-one duels and intensity have always been important parts of my game. He added with a smile: “I can probably be a bit annoying on the pitch, although my wife would say that goes for off the pitch too!” Austria’s footballer of the year in 2025, Laimer is known as a down-to-earth guy who enjoys a game of chess or a round of golf in his spare time.

Austria.strengths: Continuity: Austria’s plan has been remarkably stable for years. Rangnick has had time to imprint his ideas.
Austria.weaknesses: If the structure slips even slightly, the aggressive counter-pressing approach can leave them exposed. Pre-tournament injury to Christoph Baumgartner is a huge blow.
Austria.bio: Rangnick's high-pressing unit know exactly who they are. This is a side built not on stardom but on familiarity, trust and collective movement.

Jordan.strengths: Will look to exploit quick transitions and the pace of star winger Mousa Al-Taamari.
Jordan.weaknesses: Injury has ruled out key striker Yazan A-Naimat, leaving a huge hole in attack. Big-game experience is in short supply.
Jordan.bio: A first finals appearance for a team who qualified with a match to spare. Will likely sit deep in a back five.

playerToWatchData.name: Luis Díaz
playerToWatchData.bio: Anyone who watches the strong and combative Díaz play for Bayern would not think that he was once placed on a special diet in order to put on 10kg. That was at Barranquilla FC, a feeder club for Atlético Junior, where he came recommended by the legendary Carlos Valderrama. ‘El Pibe’ spotted him playing for Colombia at a Copa América for indigenous communities in 2015, where John Jairo Díaz was the coach. “Valderrama was practically my boss,” the coach said. “He would say: ‘That skinny kid is going to play, he’ll make it as a pro’. And look what happened.” Díaz’s father, Mane, was another key person in his career. Mane’s kidnapping by armed guerrillas on the Colombian-Venezuelan border, and safe return, made headline news around the world in 2023 when Díaz was playing for Liverpool, where he won the Premier League, an FA Cup and two League Cups.

Colombia.strengths: Goals shouldn't be a problem. Suárez is coming off a prolific season in Portugal with Sporting and only Argentina scored more in Conmebol qualifying.
Colombia.weaknesses: Tournament football leaves no room for the inconsistency that has become a hallmark of this side.
Colombia.bio: Experienced squad endured a rollercoaster qualifying campaign, beating Brazil and Argentina but losing to a poor Bolivia side.

playerToWatchData.name: Yoane Wissa
playerToWatchData.bio: Congolese federation on Facebook hoping for one thing: a chance to play for his country. Thirteen years later, his success in the Premier League has made him one of the greatest ambassadors of Congolese football. Accessible, humble and down to earth, Wissa’s journey has been anything but conventional. Before becoming a striker, he was a goalkeeper. His first season at Newcastle was disrupted by an injury suffered on international duty, preventing him from reaching the heights many expected after his form at Brentford, where he became the first DR Congo player to score more than 10 goals in a Premier League season. “The truth is, I’m not the most talented guy,” he once admitted. “What pushes me forward is that I love working hard – and I guess I’m not doing too badly.” Loved by Congolese supporters, who affectionately nickname him “Kovo” (“the bald one”), Wissa will carry huge expectations heading into the World Cup.

DR-Congo.strengths: Extremely difficult to break down and mentally tough as they come. Resilience defined their qualification campaign.
DR-Congo.weaknesses: Rarely dominate games and struggle to create freely in open play. Preparations have been disrupted by Ebola outbreak in country.
DR-Congo.bio: Pragmatic, detail-obsessed coach has the Leopards purring, with a united squad built around a clear collective identity.

playerToWatchData.name: Cristiano Ronaldo
playerToWatchData.bio: Cristiano Ronaldo may have chosen to play in Saudi Arabia instead of the USA but in November he was still invited to meet president Donald Trump at the White House as part of a visit by Saudi Arabia's crown prince Mohammed bin Salman. Ronaldo's sixth participation at the World Cup (the same as Messi) is unequivocal proof of his consistency, ambition, and the rage against time. So much so that no one dares to speak of an epilogue as his extraordinary career could still see him score his 1,000th goal. At 41, he manages to carry the feeling that there is still more to write, which is in line with the demanding nature he has always displayed. He is the leader, the point of reference, the bridge between generations. “Of course, I really want to win [the World Cup] but honestly it won't change my standing in football,” he told Piers Morgan.

Portugal.strengths: The core of the team is settled and the options varied and versatile. A squad still mourning Diogo Jota have a personal, collective mission.
Portugal.weaknesses: Few and far between but there's always a risk of Ronaldo's outsized influence becoming a problem.
Portugal.bio: One last hurrah for Ronaldo but last year's Nations League winners have quality throughout and lofty ambitions.

playerToWatchData.name: Abdukodir Khusanov
playerToWatchData.bio: The first Uzbek player in history to play in the English Premier League and France’s Ligue 1. Khusanov's father, Hikmat Khoshimov, also played for the national team at centre-back. At the age of 17 Khusanov signed for Energetik-BGU in Belarus, where he spent one difficult year. "In Belarus, I suffered being away from my parents,” he said. “Often there were training sessions three times a day. If there was heavy snow in winter, we would clear the field ourselves and then train." Khusanov’s career was transformed in 2023: he became an Asian champion as part of Uzbekistan’s Under-20 team in March, participated in the Under-20 World Cup in May, made his debut for the senior team in June, moved to Lens in July and became the youngest Uzbek player to appear in the Champions League in November. In January 2025 Khusanov moved to Manchester City. "This is one of the best transfers in the history of the club. He does not shy away from learning, takes training seriously and works with all his might. In short, Abdukodir is a very reliable player," said Pep Guardiola.

Uzbekistan.strengths: Qualification was built off a solid defence that includes Khusanov, with just seven goals conceded in 10 games.
Uzbekistan.weaknesses: Cannavaro was a legend as a player but his managerial career has been mixed. Goals are likely to be a problem.
Uzbekistan.bio: A historic first World Cup beckons. Cannavaro has stuck with the 5-2-3 system that powered the White Wolves through qualifying.

playerToWatchData.name: Luka Modric
playerToWatchData.bio: Two decades with the national team the once-generational player is closing in on 200 caps - an obscene number. The captain has still got it, at the age of 40, and has been a key player for Milan this season. The national team coach, Zlatko Dalic, calls him “the engine of this team”. Also the most-decorated player in Real Madrid’s history, having won 28 trophies despite only joining them shortly before his 27th birthday. Modric really is larger-than-life and his personality is complex and layered, from the war child-come-Ballon d’Or story to his legal troubles. “What people don’t realise about Luka,” said the late Tomislav Basic, one of Modric’s early coaches whom the player called his “second father”, “is that he is largely self-taught. For many days and months, this under-nourished, small kid played with the ball by himself in a parking lot by a refugee hotel, banging it against the wall and then controlling it.” This was where his trademark moves, like the outside-of-the-foot trivela or the half-turn when receiving the ball, came to be.

Croatia.strengths: Bags of experience and, as past World Cups have shown, a winning mentality. Modric remains a midfield maestro.
Croatia.weaknesses: Can the old guard still cut it? All that experience means plenty of miles in the legs and sapping temperatures ahead.
Croatia.bio: Semi-finalists in 2018 and 2022. Likely to revert to a back four after recent wing-back experiment brought mixed results

playerToWatchData.name: Harry Kane
playerToWatchData.bio: Overtook Pelé’s international scoring record last year, but it wasn’t until last summer that he finally lifted a club trophy, when Bayern won their 34th Bundesliga. “It was a weight on me,” he said. “As the years go by you start to think: ‘Is it going to happen?’” It was a rough road to the top: at 19 he was loaned to Norwich, missed a sitter on his debut, played five times, scored no goals. He also had a hard time on loan at Leicester – which partly motivated his creation of the Harry Kane Foundation, supporting mental health charities. “There wasn’t just a straight line to the top [for me]. I had to really go through some tough times. I’m learning more and more [about mental health] and for sure it’s something that I’ll really try to take on and help as much as I can when my career has finished.” In his spare time he plays golf, collects watches and plays chess, inspired by watching The Queen's Gambit. He told GQ in 2024: “Since that came out I've started to learn and I'm about 1200 rated on the 10-minute version on Chess.com. It's fairly decent.”

England.strengths: They have enviable attacking options, a host of No 10s and in Rice one of the best midfielders in the world.
England.weaknesses: There are question marks over the defensive options and, as ever, fitness concerns over key players.
England.bio: Cruised through qualifying but the opposition was hardly taxing. So it's the usual question: how will they fare when they come up against the best in a knockout tie?

playerToWatchData.name: Antoine Semenyo
playerToWatchData.bio: Arsenal, Millwall, Reading and Tottenham turned Semenyo down as a youngster, and Palace let him go at 15 after eight weeks on trial. “I’ve never been so upset in my life about football. I was crying to my dad,” he told The Guardian in 2024. “I stopped playing for a year, just focused on school.” But, via a youth academy programme he earned a trial at Bristol City in 2017 and signed his first professional contract there. He had three loans spells before establishing himself, then joined Bournemouth for £10m in 2023, and Man City for £64m in January. “Sometimes I get memories flash up on my phone from when I was out on loan, and I compare them with now,” he said. “You go on a trip down memory lane and it is like: ‘Wow, you’ve come a long way.’” He has the word ‘chosen’ tattooed on his back. He told GQ: “I looked at [basketballer] Jayson Tatum's tattoos – he has the name of the street he grew up on and other stuff, and it said ‘chosen’ on his back. I was like, you know what? This resembles me. I feel like the chosen one, I feel like God's chosen me to be in this position.”

Ghana.strengths: Have developed into a major threat from set pieces and in Semenyo the Black Stars have one of the most in-form attackers in European club football.
Ghana.weaknesses: Lack of elite defenders is a worry and goalkeeping unit lacks international experience.
Ghana.bio: A team littered with attacking talent that cruised through qualifying but their recent run of defeats is a concern.

Panama.strengths: Squad has been together a long time, has pace and is full of confidence. Solid recent showings in Gold Cup and Nations League.
Panama.weaknesses: Tend to struggle against the bigger teams and several key players are now well into their 30s.
Panama.bio: La Marea Roja are hopeful of improving upon hapless 2018 showing after long development under former Leeds coach.
